On Ravi's point about immutable logs and provenance attestations: from my side, the persistent release runners are the ones that would be executing production release builds, so if those requirements apply to regulated release repositories, the runners running those jobs — the two persistent ones — would need to be configured to produce the signed provenance attestations and route logs to immutable storage. transcript.text: On the capacity question Maya raised — whether the two persistent release runners count within the 32-job ceiling — I can speak to that now. The 32-concurrent-job safe production ceiling I measured this morning reflects the total capacity of the ephemeral runner pool specifically. The two isolated persistent runners Owen described are a separate, distinct pool running on their own infrastructure, so they would not draw against that 32-job ceiling. That said, we should be deliberate about how we set the policy's concurrency limit. The measured campaign-day burst was 28 simultaneous jobs on the ephemeral pool, the safe ceiling is 32, and the alert threshold needs to fire at 24 to give us enough lead time before we hit the hard limit. If we set the policy concurrency limit at 20 as currently drafted, we'd be throttling well below the 28 jobs we've actually observed in production, which would cause queue backlogs on campaign days. I'd recommend setting the concurrency limit to at least 28 to accommodate observed demand, keeping the alert at 24, and treating 32 as the hard ceiling that triggers protective throttling. I still need to add these measurements to the capacity dashboard so the team has visibility — I'll do that as part of this rollout. On Ravi's scope question, I don't have visibility into whether the immutable log and provenance requirements extend beyond regulated release repos, so I'll defer to Ravi on that. But from an SRE perspective, if those requirements do apply to the persistent release runners, we'll need to make sure the log routing and attestation pipeline are in place before those runners go live.

transcript.text: Thanks Owen and Lena for addressing those dependencies. Let me clarify the scope of the compliance requirements, since both of you flagged that as an open question. That means Owen's two isolated persistent release runners are exactly the runners that need these controls configured, since those are the ones executing production release builds for regulated repos. Non-regulated CI jobs running on the ephemeral pool would not need immutable log storage or provenance attestations under the current compliance framework. So the dependency is scoped: the persistent release runners need immutable log routing and signed provenance attestation generation before they go live, and the policy needs to specify 180-day immutable retention and provenance attestations for regulated release builds specifically. I still need to open the compliance ticket to formally document these requirements — I'll do that as part of this rollout so we have a tracked record for the audit. One thing I want to flag: since the persistent release runners are the ones handling regulated releases, we should make sure the policy language ties the immutable log and attestation requirements to those runners and those repositories explicitly, rather than applying them broadly to all jobs, which would create unnecessary overhead on the ephemeral pool.
